name: gentle-202
title: System Design Interview - An insiders guide volume 3

blocks.text: This section talks about searching for phrases that start with 'di' and how the system handles these searches.
When a user types part of a word starting with 'di', the system shows possible completions.
The system needs to manage a lot of searches every second.
Here are some important numbers about how many searches happen:

Metric | Value
~24,000 query per second (QPS) | This is the normal rate of searches.
10,000,000 users | Total number of users.
10 queries per day | Each user does several searches.
20 characters | Average length of each search query.
24 hours | Every day runs for 24 hours.
3600 seconds | Total seconds in an hour.
At peak times, the search queries can double. This means:
Every day, 20% of the searches are new ones.
This leads to new data being added to the system.
Here's how to calculate the new data each day:
New Data = 10 million * 10 queries / day * 20 bytes per query * 20% = 0.4 GB
So, 0.4GB of new data is added to storage every day.

script:
Each search tells us something. We need to review them. Searching for phrases is common. For example, when a user types 'di', potential completions show up. They might see 'di', 'din', 'dinn', 'dinne', and 'dinner'. Each of those queries matters. They help us understand user behavior.

Let’s calculate the daily data handled. We have around 24,000 queries every second. That's our normal rate. With 10 million users doing about 10 queries each day, that’s a lot of activity. Each query takes 20 bytes. 24,000 queries, multiplied by seconds in a day, shows us the total.

Now, let’s discuss the implications of this data. At peak times, the number of search queries can double, reaching about 48,000 queries per second. Every day, around 20% of the searches are new. This leads to new data. So, when we calculate the new data, we find that 0.4 gigabytes is added daily. This means we need storage that grows quickly. We’ve got to be prepared for that.
